run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T19:37:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is backed by real frontend failures: frontend spans carried no ERROR status until ~19:36:37, then ERROR spans appeared through ~19:44, peaking at a 5-minute increase of about 544 error spans and a 7.9% error-span ratio at 19:40 (trace-span counts, not request counts). The errors are HTTP 500s produced by two downstream call paths only: frontend -> ad (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE) and frontend -> checkout -> payment (oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, gRPC 14). Both failed with TCP 'connect: connection refused' to the services' own ClusterIPs (ad 100.65.180.246:8080, payment 100.70.188.60:8080). Cart, product-catalog, currency, quote, shipping and recommendation calls in the same traces were successful. In the minute before the burst, Deployments ad and payment were both rolled out at 2026-11-17T19:35:31Z (new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665, old ReplicaSets scaled to 0, old pods killed 19:35:34/35, new pods Started 19:35:33/34) with the same image tags and the same service targetPort/container port 8080, so this was a configuration-only rollout; what actually changed in the pod template is not observable. The flagd-config ConfigMap currently holds two enabled fault-injection settings whose names refer to exactly the two failing services (adFailure defaultVariant 'on', paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%'), while the unavailability-related flag paymentUnreachable is 'off'; this is the leading candidate, but the observed mechanism (TCP connection refused) does not match those flags' own descriptions, and the errors stopped around 19:44 while both flags are still on, so the attribution is not proven.

claims.text: frontend recorded zero ERROR spans through the sample at 19:36:55 and then an error burst: the 2-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 121.3 at 19:36:55, peaked at 544 at 19:37:55, stayed 200-400 per 2 minutes through 19:43:55, and returned to 0 from 19:44:55 onward.

At 19:40 the frontend error spans were confined to two call paths: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had 216.2 error spans vs 47.2 non-error spans in the preceding 5 minutes, and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder had 48.3 error vs 121.9 non-error; grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and RecommendationService/ListRecommendations had 0 error spans in the same window.

The failed frontend requests returned http.status_code 500 with error details naming TCP refusals: '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, and '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' on POST /api/checkout / executing api route (pages) /api/checkout.

The refused addresses are the demo Services' own ClusterIPs: Service ad has clusterIP 100.65.180.246 port 8080 targetPort 8080 and Service payment has clusterIP 100.70.188.60 port 8080 targetPort 8080.

Deployments ad and payment were both rolled out at 2026-11-17T19:35:31Z: events record 'Scaled up replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled up replica set payment-9c8ffb665 from 0 to 1' at 19:35:31, 'Started container ad' 19:35:33 and 'Started container payment' 19:35:34, 'Deleted pod: ad-554b849958-mbnxm' / 'Stopping container ad' 19:35:34, 'Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb' / 'Stopping container payment' 19:35:35, and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' / 'payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0'.

The ad and payment replica sets confirm a configuration-style replacement: ad-554b849958 (created 2026-11-17T19:01:47Z, now 0 replicas) and ad-6cb57f76d (created 2026-11-17T19:35:31Z, 1 ready) both run image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, and payment-55766d76b9 (19:01:46Z, 0 replicas) and payment-9c8ffb665 (19:35:31Z, 1 ready) both run ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.

The replacement pods are healthy as objects: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (started 19:35:31Z) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (started 19:35:31Z) are Running and Ready (Ready condition 19:35:34Z / 19:35:35Z), restartCount 0, expose containerPort 8080, and declare no readinessProbe; their Deployment envs are AD_PORT=8080 and PAYMENT_PORT=8080 with FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013.

The two dependency services themselves emitted no error spans during the burst: at 19:40, traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="ad",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} and {service_name="payment",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} were both 0, while checkout carried 79.2 error spans, exclusively on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config currently holds enabled fault-injection settings that name exactly the two failing services: "adFailure" with description "Fail ad service", state ENABLED, defaultVariant "on"; and "paymentFailure" with description "Fail payment service charge requests n%", state ENABLED, defaultVariant "100%" (variant value 1).

Other flags in the same ConfigMap are off, including "paymentUnreachable" (description "Payment service is unavailable", defaultVariant "off") and cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and emailMemoryLeak (defaultVariant "off").

The 500s propagated through the request chain visible in the same traces: load-generator POST spans, frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans and frontend spans all carry error=true with http.status_code 500, while cart HGET/GetCart, currency Convert, quote calculate-quote, shipping /get-quote and product-catalog GetProduct spans in those traces have no error status.
The frontend pod itself was not restarted or replaced: frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-17T19:01:48Z.

Error magnitude at the peak, measured on spans: at 19:40 the ratio of ERROR to total frontend spans over the preceding 5 minutes was 0.0789 (7.9%), versus zero frontend ERROR spans before 19:36:37 in the same metric.

The new ad and payment pods were serving normally by 19:43-19:45: payment logs from 19:43:32Z show repeated 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs, and ad logs from 19:44:10Z show normal 'Targeted ad request received' handling; the Services' Endpoints now list only the new pods (ad 100.96.4.142, payment 100.96.4.221) on port 8080.

Leading hypothesis: the fault-injection settings held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure="on", paymentFailure="100%") are the injected fault behind the frontend's 500s, with the ad and payment pod replacements at 19:35:31Z as the mechanism by which the change took effect and the resulting connection refusals to the ad and payment ClusterIPs as its consequences. This is consistent with the two failing services matching the two enabled flags one-for-one and with the burst beginning about one minute after the rollout, but it is not proven (see counter-evidence and gaps).

Competing hypothesis that remains open: the configuration-only rollouts of Deployments ad and payment at 19:35:31Z (new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665, old pods deleted) left the two Services without a working backend for roughly 19:36:37-19:44, producing the ECONNREFUSED failures at their ClusterIPs; under this reading the rollout itself is the proximate change and the flag settings are background configuration. The trigger of those rollouts could not be identified from the available data sources.

The observed failure mode does not match the enabled flags' own descriptions: the spans report TCP 'connect: connection refused' to the ad and payment ClusterIPs (no listener at the target port), whereas adFailure is described as 'Fail ad service' and paymentFailure as 'Fail payment service charge requests n%' (request-level failure), and the flag whose description does match service unavailability, paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), is 'off' in the same ConfigMap.

The errors do not track the flag state within the observed window: frontend ERROR spans are 0 from 19:27 through 19:36:55, run 19:36:37-~19:44, and are 0 again from 19:44:55, while adFailure='on' and paymentFailure='100%' are still the values in effect when the ConfigMap was read at ~19:53.

The ad and payment workloads are not themselves failing now and show no server-side errors: both pods are Ready with restartCount 0, ad and payment ERROR span counts were 0 during the burst, payment logs at 19:43-19:45 show successful charge/complete pairs, ad logs at 19:44+ show normal request handling, and the Services' Endpoints list the new pods on port 8080.

Rejected: the frontend pod failed or was replaced. frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 has startTime 19:01:48Z, restartCount 0, is Ready, and its ERROR spans are client-side failures of calls to ad and payment that returned 500 to callers.

Rejected: cart, currency, quote, shipping, product-catalog or recommendation were part of this failure. In the failing traces their spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code="0" / otel.status_code="OK" or no error status, frontend had 0 ERROR spans on its cart, product and recommendation operations at 19:40, and cart's own error-span count was 0.

Retrieve the change history/audit log for Deployments ad and payment and for ConfigMap flagd-config around 2026-11-17T19:35Z (the change_history integration is not available in this Run) to identify who applied the rollout and when the adFailure/paymentFailure values were set.

If the fault injection is no longer intended, set adFailure to 'off' and paymentFailure to 'off'/'0%' in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config and confirm the frontend error rate stays at its pre-19:36 level; meanwhile add readinessProbes to the ad and payment containers (none are declared) so a rollout cannot route traffic to a pod before it accepts connections.

gaps: No change-history source is integrated in this Run, so the actor, method and stated reason for the 19:35:31Z rollouts of Deployments ad and payment, and the time at which flagd-config's adFailure/paymentFailure values were set, are unknown.

The previous pod template of the ad and payment Deployments is not observable (old ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 are scaled to 0 and their pods were deleted), so which template field changed at 19:35:31Z could not be determined; a query for kube_pod_container_info at 19:50Z returned no data, so image digests could not be compared (only the identical image tags 2.1.3-ad / 2.1.3-payment were visible).

The declared fault itself was not observed: no ad-service or payment-service error span, log line or gRPC application error status is present in the evidence, only TCP connection refusals seen by callers.

The alert's own metric could not be reproduced: a query for http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{service_name="frontend"} returned no data, so the reported value 2.5777777777777775 is unverified; error magnitude here is derived from traces_span_metrics_calls_total span counts.

Prometheus samples for traces_span_metrics_calls_total start at 2026-11-17T19:14:05Z in the returned windows, so there is no baseline before 19:14 and the pre-existing ad/payment traffic level is only partially observed.

The trace backend view for frontend was truncated and covered traces only around 19:36:37-19:36:40, so the rest of the error window (to ~19:44) is known only from aggregated span metrics, not from individual traces.
Application log coverage is partial: ad and payment container logs were only readable from about 19:44:10Z and 19:43:32Z respectively, and the frontend log query for error lines returned no data.
Container logs for the flagd pod (flagd, flagd-ui, init-config) returned no data, so no flag-evaluation or flag-update record was available.
A networkpolicy query in otel-demo returned no data, so network policy state at incident time is unknown.
next_steps: Pull Kubernetes audit/change records for the otel-demo namespace covering 2026-11-17T19:30Z-19:45Z, specifically Deployment ad, Deployment payment and ConfigMap flagd-config.
Compare the old replica sets' pod templates (if recoverable from audit history or a backup) with ad-6cb57f76d / payment-9c8ffb665 to see which configuration field changed at 19:35:31Z.
Review flagd evaluation logs or the flagd-ui change feed to establish when adFailure and paymentFailure were switched from off to on.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
